messages:
megan_sales: Quick heads-up 52 MedBridge just returned our security questionnaire for the Private deployment POC. They want a short connectivity playbook: PrivateLink vs peering, static egress for allowlist, firewall rules including FQDNs, TLS inspection impact on SDKs, and any compliance blockers (HIPAA/SOC2). Can we draft a concise pack?

diego_neteng: TL;DR: Recommend PrivateLink (AWS) / Private Endpoint (Azure) for POCs. Less lateral exposure than peering. If they insist on peering, call out that peering opens routing between VPCs and needs strict SG/NACLs.

ben_solutions: Static egress: preferred pattern is customer-managed NAT + EIP(s). That gives customer control for allowlisting with their partners. Redwood can provide reserved egress IPs as an addon, but provisioning lead time and a small monthly fee apply. For a short POC, ask them to provide EIPs to speed things up.

tara_sec: Compliance note: for HIPAA customers we recommend customer-owned egress so PHI egress is auditable under their control. If they ask us to manage egress IPs or to enable TLS MITM, we'll need a scoped compliance review and MSA amendment. Also mention BYOK/KMS options for Private deployments.

diego_neteng: Firewall snippet to hand to customer (paste into ticket):
```
Allow inbound from Redwood connector (PrivateLink / peer):
- TCP 443 -> <endpoint ENI IPs> (required for API)
- TCP 80 -> optional (health checks)
- UDP 123 -> optional (NTP)
- ICMP echo -> optional (diagnostics)
If using peering: add route table entry for Redwood peering CIDR and restrict SGs to only the service subnets.
If FQDN allowlist required: api.redwood-inference.net, telemetry.redwood-inference.net (note: FQDNs rely on DNS resolution; prefer IPs for PrivateLink).
```

ben_solutions: Also call out SNI behaviour: some customers doing TLS inspect will break SNI-based routing and SDK certificate pinning. Recommend they run a customer-side forward proxy for inspection.

megan_sales: Pricing asked by customer: two static egress IPs for 6-week POC, any quick number?

provisioning-bot: Quick estimate: Reserved Egress addon = prorated monthly base + per-IP charge. Finance to confirm numbers; typical POC pricing escalates if we reserve infrastructure.

megan_sales: I'll flag to the customer that customer-managed EIPs is fastest; we'll only offer Redwood-reserved IPs if they explicitly request and sign the addon.

tara_sec: DDoS note: volumetric protection should be their cloud provider (AWS Shield / Azure DDoS). Redwood provides per-route throttling and application-level rate-limits but not managed scrubbing. Include this in the questionnaire response.

diego_neteng: Blockers before kickoff:
- customer network diagram (subnets, NAT, route tables)
- decision who owns egress IPs
- security contact and answers about TLS inspect and cert pinning
- IAM approvals if we need to create ENIs in their account for PrivateLink
- allowlist entries (their EIPs or Redwood EIPs)

ben_solutions: Action items: I'll draft a one-page connectivity one-pager + a simple network diagram for AWS/Azure variants. @diego_neteng can add exact CIDR/EIP ranges we'll publish for allowlisting.

diego_neteng: I'll produce an allowlist email template and the CIDR list by EOB tomorrow.

tara_sec: I'll prepare a short HIPAA/SOC2 blurb and TLS inspection guidance for the questionnaire.

megan_sales: Great 52 please keep the language customer-friendly. I'll send the pack to MedBridge after we have the one-pager. Any other gotchas?

diego_neteng: If they require Redwood to manage static egress + TLS inspection inside our environment, expect a 2-4 week compliance and provisioning timeline.

megan_sales: Noted. Closing for now; will reopen if MedBridge asks for in-platform TLS MITM. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
